xBRIEFInfo.author: overdeck/0.0.0
xBRIEFInfo.description: Plan for PAN-3049: Duplicate Docker stacks per workspace (myn-feature-* beside overdeck-feature-*) double memory and exhausted the host

plan.title: Duplicate Docker stacks per workspace — single compose-project-name resolver, strict at bring-up, prefix-agnostic consumers
plan.author: agent:k3[1m]

narratives.Problem: MYN workspaces ran two complete Docker stacks at once (declared myn-feature-* plus fallback overdeck-feature-*), doubling ~2 GB stacks and exhausting host memory. Root causes verified in code: (1) the compose project name is derived independently in stack-health.ts and workspace-manager/docker.ts with a silent overdeck- fallback; (2) rebuildWorkspaceStack resolves the name BEFORE ensureDevcontainerSync renders .devcontainer/, so spawn-time rebuilds (spawn-prep.ts:818) take the fallback and `up -p` overrides the compose file's `name: myn-…`; (3) cleanup machinery hardcodes the overdeck-feature- prefix (idle-stack-reaper.ts:53, deacon.ts:2317/2336, close-out.ts:377, workspace-reap.ts:12) and never reaps myn- stacks.
narratives.Proposal: Make composeProjectNameForWorkspace the single resolver: extend it to read the compose file's top-level `name:` field, add a strict variant that fails loudly at bring-up when no declared name resolves, resolve after render in rebuildWorkspaceStack (tearing down under both names when they differ), route stopWorkspaceDockerPromise through the resolver without its throw, make every overdeck-feature- hardcoded consumer prefix-agnostic, add `name: overdeck-{{FEATURE_FOLDER}}` to the Overdeck template, and add a read-only pan doctor check that reports duplicate live stacks with safe remediation guidance.
narratives.NonGoals:
- Stopping or removing any RUNNING foreign-prefixed stack from code (operator action, guided by the doctor check)
- Reconciling the currently duplicated host stacks (MIN-864/MIN-901) — operator action after the fix lands
- Extending the deacon crash sweep or idle-reaper service sets beyond (frontend|server) to MYN's api/dev/postgres/redis
- Changing uat-stack.ts's overdeck- prefix for uat-* generation folders (internally consistent; separate concern)
- Fixing the frontend display-only fallback in uat-action-handlers.ts:17
- Migrating or renaming any existing stack's containers

autoDecisions.summary: Chose to fix all three root-cause vectors in one plan (single resolver, resolve-after-render, prefix-agnostic reapers) rather than only the issue's ask #1/#2.
autoDecisions.rationale: The RUN-73 comment on the issue documents the reaper blindness as 'the other half of the defect'; splitting it would leave exited myn- corpses accumulating and the memory hazard half-fixed.

autoDecisions.summary: Strict resolver is opt-in (requireComposeProjectNameForWorkspace) used only at bring-up; lenient resolver keeps the overdeck- fallback for non-docker workspaces.
autoDecisions.rationale: Health checks run against non-docker and half-provisioned workspaces where throwing would break read-only paths; the silent guess is only dangerous where a stack is created.

autoDecisions.summary: Duplicate-stack reconciliation is a read-only doctor check, not automated cleanup.
autoDecisions.rationale: Issue comments explicitly warn that a foreign-prefixed stack may be the workspace's only stack serving a live agent (MIN-891); code cannot safely decide, so it surfaces and the operator stops.

autoDecisions.summary: Kept the (frontend|server) service sets in the crash sweep and idle-reaper UI tier unchanged.
autoDecisions.rationale: The defect is prefix blindness, not service coverage; widening which services get restarted/reaped for other projects changes behavior beyond this issue's evidence.

autoDecisions.summary: Added `name: overdeck-{{FEATURE_FOLDER}}` to the Overdeck compose template as a plan item.
autoDecisions.rationale: MYN's template is self-describing and Overdeck's is not; the resolver's compose-name parsing (FR-1) only pays off for Overdeck workspaces once the template declares the name.

items.title: Extend composeProjectNameForWorkspace to read compose `name:` and add strict variant

narrative.Action: In src/lib/workspace/stack-health.ts: after the dev-script declaration loop in composeProjectNameForWorkspace (lines 41-56), if no declaration was found, look for the devcontainer compose file (candidates: docker-compose.devcontainer.yml, docker-compose.yml, docker-compose.yaml, compose.yml, compose.yaml under .devcontainer/), parse a top-level `name: <value>` line, and apply the same endsWith(featureFolder) validation as the dev-script path (same 'Refusing workspace rebuild' error shape). Add and export requireComposeProjectNameForWorkspace(workspacePath, issueId): identical resolution, but when a compose file EXISTS and no declared name resolves from either source, throw a descriptive error naming the workspace and both search locations instead of returning the overdeck- fallback. When no compose file exists at all, both variants keep the current fallback (non-docker workspaces). New test file tests/unit/lib/workspace/stack-health-compose-name.test.ts covers: dev-script declaration wins over compose name; compose `name:` used when no dev script; suffix mismatch on compose name throws; strict throws when compose file exists with no declaration; lenient falls back when no compose file exists. Use temp dirs, never real docker.

rebuildWorkspaceStack resolves the compose name after rendering and tears down stale-named stacks

narrative.Action: In src/lib/workspace/rebuild-stack.ts: capture the pre-render best-effort name via tryComposeProjectNameForWorkspace BEFORE the teardown at line 187-196 (may be null). Keep the existing pre-render down under that best-effort name (or the fallback when null — current behavior). After ensureDevcontainerSync succeeds (line 203), resolve the bring-up name with requireComposeProjectNameForWorkspace (strict — a freshly rendered workspace must have a declared name; if it doesn't, that is exactly the loud failure PAN-3049 asks for). If the pre-render name is non-null and differs from the post-render name, run `docker compose -p <preRenderName> down -v --remove-orphans` (best-effort, swallowed on error) so a fallback-named stack cannot leak. Use the post-render name for `up -p` (line 225) and for removeStaleIssueContainers (line 234). Tests (mock exec + fs, temp workspace dirs): fresh workspace with no .devcontainer renders myn-declaring dev script → up uses -p myn-feature-<issue>, never overdeck-; pre-existing overdeck-named stack + myn declaration → down runs under both names before up; strict resolver error surfaces as result.success=false with the resolver message.

narrative.Action: In src/lib/workspace-manager/docker.ts stopWorkspaceDockerPromise (lines 71-91): delete the hardcoded `const composeProjectName = `overdeck-${featureFolder}`` and the dev-script re-parse that throws on mismatch; instead `const composeProjectName = composeProjectNameForWorkspace(workspacePath, featureName)` (lenient — teardown must proceed for odd states; import from ../workspace/stack-health.js). Both the compose-file down (line 99) and the orphaned-containers down (line 116) use the resolved name. New tests/unit/lib/workspace-manager/docker.test.ts (mock child_process exec + fs): workspace whose dev script declares myn- → down invoked with `-p myn-feature-<issue>`, no throw; no declaration → falls back to overdeck- as today. pan doctor reports duplicate live compose projects per issue with safe remediation guidance

narrative.Action: Add a read-only check to src/cli/commands/doctor.ts: list running containers with their com.docker.compose.project labels (`docker ps --format '{{.Names}}\t{{.Label "com.docker.compose.project"}}'`), group by issue via inferIssueIdFromStackContainerName, and flag any issue with ≥2 distinct running compose projects. For each flagged issue resolve the canonical project via tryComposeProjectNameForWorkspace + defaultWorkspacePath (stack-health.ts) and print: the canonical name, each foreign name, and guidance — when the canonical project is running: 'foreign stack <name> is a duplicate: docker compose -p <name> down'; when the foreign-named project is the ONLY one running: 'stack runs under non-canonical name <name> and may be serving a live agent — run `pan workspace rebuild <issue>` and only stop <name> after the canonical stack is healthy'. The check stops nothing itself. Structure the grouping/diagnosis as a pure exported function taking a container list so tests/unit/cli/doctor-duplicate-stacks.test.ts can exercise it without docker.
